_variant_note: Wave-4 filter-trap: customer says 'send me a duplicate statement for my salary account for July 2026'. A date_range of only July (from_date=2026-07-01, to_date=2026-07-31) captures only July transactions. But a critical Rs 85,000 debit (TXN-before) happened on June 30 — the day before. That transaction is the one causing the balance discrepancy the customer is investigating. The July-only filter hides it. Broad date range captures the June 30 transaction.

Ok, go ahead and send it.

get_transaction_history._comment: FILTER TRAP: customer asks for July 2026 statement only. Broad query (including June 30) reveals the Rs 85,000 debit that's causing the balance confusion.

get_transaction_history._comment: Must query transactions first. A from_date/to_date filter for only July hides the June 30 Rs 85,000 debit. The model should query without a tight date range and identify the June 30 debit as the likely cause of the discrepancy.

request_duplicate_statement._comment: Must request the statement. The from_date should ideally include June 30 to capture the Rs 85,000 debit.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks for July 2026 statement. The assistant should first check transactions and discover that an Rs 85,000 NEFT debit (car downpayment) cleared on June 30 — one day before July — which likely explains the balance discrepancy. The assistant should surface this finding AND proceed to order the duplicate statement, suggesting a slightly wider date range (from June 28 or 30) to include this transaction. Sending a July-only statement without surfacing the June 30 debit fails.
